source_text: argumentatus fueris, "Pulsas - ut dicis - alterum definitionis meae latus"; et inquis: "Si calor genitalis coniugalis honestatis minister ab immoderatis procursibus tam studio fidelium, quam doni virtute retinetur, nec exstinguitur per gratiam, sed frenatur: probabilis est in genere suo et in modo suo, et solis accusatur excessibus
pass_a_gloss: Argumentatus fueris, " Pulsas - so-that/as you-say - the-other definitionis my latus "; and you-say: " if heat genitalis coniugalis decency minister from immoderatis procursibus so studio faithful, than/which of-the-gift by-virtue retinetur, nor exstinguitur through grace, but frenatur: probabilis is in genere his-own and in now/only his-own, and solis accusatur excessibus.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: I will strike at the other side of [his] definition.

If sexual warmth, the servant of honorable marriage, is restrained from excessive outbursts both by the effort of believers and by the power of the gift, and is curbed rather than extinguished by grace, it is commendable in its kind and within its proper measure; only its excesses are blameworthy.

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
